definitions.plain_definition: A rule from physics that says erasing information always produces a tiny amount of heat, meaning information can't be perfectly preserved forever.
definitions.used_in_context: Information degrades over time. That's not opinion — it's Landauer's Principle and the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

definitions.plain_definition: A law of physics that says things naturally become more disordered over time, like a room getting messy without anyone cleaning it.
definitions.used_in_context: Information degrades over time. That's not opinion — it's Landauer's Principle and the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

definitions.plain_definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system; the more entropy, the more chaotic things are.
definitions.used_in_context: Every century of transmission increases entropy.

definitions.plain_definition: How well something holds together without falling apart or losing its original meaning; in this context, how well a text stays accurate over time.
definitions.used_in_context: The Bible's answer breaks information theory. Enter your challenger below.

definitions.plain_definition: A number calculated to show how well a text has survived the forces that would normally make it fall apart.
definitions.used_in_context: The Coherence Score is a composite of six stress factors that any text must survive.

definitions.plain_definition: The study of how information is stored, sent, and how much can be lost without ruining the message.
definitions.used_in_context: Watch the information theory do its work.

definitions.plain_definition: How well a message stays the same as it is passed from person to person or copy to copy over time.
definitions.used_in_context: Compare its transmission coherence to the Bible.

definitions.plain_definition: Things that make it harder for a text to stay accurate, like age, number of translations, or time between copies.
definitions.used_in_context: The Coherence Score is a composite of six stress factors that any text must survive.

definitions.plain_definition: The percentage of words or sentences that are the same when comparing different copies of the same text.
The amount of time between when a text was first written and the oldest copy we still have today.
A statistical measure of how far something is from what you'd expect; a higher number means it's more surprising.
The amount of disorder you would predict based on things like age and number of translations.
A number that compares how well one text holds together compared to another.
The pressure that tends to make something more disordered; in this case, the forces that would make a text lose its original meaning.
definitions.used_in_context: the Bible was under far greater entropic stress

definitions.plain_definition: How strong or clear the original message is, even after being passed through many copies or translations.
definitions.used_in_context: Equal coherence under greater stress means greater underlying signal strength.
